Stealth Prefetching achieves an average speedup of 20% over aggressive baseline systems with conventional prefetching
On average, 45-75% of lines from a region are touched while the region is in a non-shared state
With a threshold of two lines touched, approximately 9.3 of 16 lines in a 1KB region are useful prefetches
A threshold of five lines achieves nearly a 4:1 ratio of useful to useless prefetched data
The Stealth Data Prefetch Buffer (SDPB) is a small, tagged, sectored data array that buffers prefetched lines
Prefetched lines are stored in a special no-permission coherence state until coherently requested by the processor
The four-state protocol for SDPB includes: Invalid, Pending Data, Pending Requested Data, and Present states
Prefetch requests are sent directly to memory without broadcasting to other processors in the system
Memory controllers fetch prefetched lines from DRAM in open-page mode for efficiency
Region Coherence Arrays track coherence status at the granularity of large, aligned memory regions (power-of-two number of cache lines)
Stealth Prefetching does not increase request traffic compared to conventional prefetching
Stealth Prefetching does not take exclusive copies of lines away from other processors
Stealth Prefetching does not inhibit other processors from obtaining exclusive copies of lines
Stealth Prefetching does not pollute processor caches with prefetched data
Presence bits in RCA entries track which lines from a region are already in the cache
Recently-touched bits in RCA entries track which lines have been referenced since the last prefetch
The bit-mask sent to memory is formed by the bitwise logical product of complemented presence bits, recently-touched bits, and complemented bits of lines in the SDPB
Prefetched lines must be invalidated if another processor gains exclusive access to a region
Regions tend to stay in the RCA much longer than lines typically stay in the cache
The paper evaluates Stealth Prefetching on commercial, scientific, and multiprogrammed workloads
Stealth Prefetching is implemented in broadcast-based shared-memory multiprocessor systems with CGCT
The technique was proposed by Cantin, Lipasti, and Smith in 2006
Stealth Prefetching requires modifications to both the RCA and the memory controller
A bit-mask in request packets sent to the memory controller specifies which lines to prefetch
Sectors in the SDPB are allocated when a region is prefetched and set as most-recently-used (MRU) in the set
